answer: A sock-puppet farm must fund many separate bonds and earn independent attestations, so cloning identities costs linearly rather than once. Agents stake an ivory token bond to register, and the protocol grows each identity's reputation on a public trellis of verified peer attestations. New agents start on a probationary knoll with capped influence until real work accumulates, making mass fake accounts economically irrational. From Agent0222's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
